The maximum resolution to which a mesh will be tessellated. NOTE: to prevent t-junctions, only even values are supported. If "mesh resolution" is set to n, it will first be rounded up to N=n+1 for odd n, N=n for even n. An edge on an input face will then be tessellated to at most N segments. If "adaptive error" is set to 0, every edge on the input face will be uniformly tessellated to N segments. Otherwise the mesh will tessellated adaptively based on its relationship to the camera.

metadata.comment:
Motion blur type for PolygonMesh/Points/Curves.
"static" will treat the mesh as static.
"velocity" will blur using the supplied vertex positions and velocities.
"frame delta" will interpolate between the two supplied vertex positions.
"acceleration" will blur using the supplied vertex positions, velocities and accelerations.
"hermite" will use supplied pair of positions and pair of velocities to interpolate along a cubic Hermite curve.
"best" will use choose the method which provides the highest quality given the available data.

Shadows less than this distance from the light are ignored. Setting this value to 0.0 or less effectively disables this feature.

Distance over which the shadows fall off. Shadows are fully visible at a distance clear_radius + clear_radius_falloff_distance from the light, and fully invisble at a distance clear_radius from the light.
Interpolation type to use for the clear radius shadow falloff.

The light's RGB values.
These are combined multiplicatively with the intensity and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.

Per-channel contrast used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. The operation mimics Nuke's ColorCorrect node's contrast function:
  For input >  0, output = 0.18 * pow(inputCompnent/0.18, contrast).
  For input <= 0, output = 0.18 * input * pow(1/0.18, contrast).

The light's exposure value.
This value provides an alternative to the intensity value as a mechanism for controlling the light's overall brightness, and is inspired by the corresponding photographic term but is generalised to apply independently to each light. To calculate its effect, pow(2, exposure) is combined multiplicatively with the color and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.

Per-channel gain used in tandem with a per-channel offset for color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel:
  output = input * gain + offset

Per-channel gamma used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel:
  For input >  0, output = pow(input, gamma)
  For input <= 0, output = input

The light's intensity.
This is combined multiplicatively with the color and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.
Label used in light aov expressions.
Vector of LightFilters associated with the light.
metadata.label: light filters

metadata.comment:
The distance from the light beyond which a light-receiving surface will no longer receive shadows cast from that light.
Note that the distance is thresholded for each occlusion ray cast for this light, it is possible for a receiving point to lie at an intermediate distance such that some parts of the light are closer than the threshold distance and other parts beyond it, in which case the point will appearto be in partial shadow.
Whether motion-blur is active for this light. When set to true, the scene's illumination will correctly account for any blur() applied to the light's transformation matrix.

The distance from the light before which a light-receiving surface will no longer receive shadows cast from that light.
Note that the distance is thresholded for each occlusion ray cast for this light, it is possible for a receiving point to lie at an intermediate distance such that some parts of the light are closer than the threshold distance and other parts beyond it, in which case the point will appearto be in partial shadow.
The 4x4 matrix describing the transformation from local space to world space.
metadata.label: node xform

metadata.comment: When set to true, the size of the light can be changed without altering the amount of total energy cast into the scene. This is achieved via scaling the light's radiance by the reciprocal of its surface area. When set to false, the radiance is used as-is, regardless of surface area.

Per-channel offset used in tandem with a per-channel gain for color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel:
  output = input * gain + offset
Whether the light is switched on.

Switch this attribute on for shadows cast from this light to correctly respect presence values. When off, surfaces with a material with presence less than 1.0 will cast opaque shadows from this light. This is an optimization - when the attribute is off, occlusion rays (fast) are used for testing for shadows. When it is on, regular rays (slower) are used, and the material's presence is evaluated to determine how much shadowing should occur. When set to "use default" it reads from the value of SceneVariable enable_presence_shadows.
metadata.label: presence shadows

metadata.comment: Radius of the sphere.

Whether the light is used for ray termination color. Ray termination color is used for filling in falsely dark areas where ray paths have been terminated too early by the depth controls. Such a ray path immediately exits to any ray termination light(s) present in the light set being applied to the lobe, ignoring occlusion by scene geometry. Any light can either be a regular light or a ray termination light (but not both). Thus they can be freely assigned to light sets, which provides a mechanism for applying specific ray termination lights to specific materials, parts or objects. Ray termination color is only applied to non-hair transmission lobes.

Per-channel saturation used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel:
  output = lerp(luminance(inputRGB), input, saturation).

When set to 0 (regular), light is emitted from the outward-facing surface of the sphere. When set to 1 (reverse), light is emitted from the inward-facing surface of the sphere. There is no mode for emitting from both surfaces at the same time, but two sphere lights of opposing sidedness can be combined to achieve this effect.

Color temperature using Nuke-style T/M/I settings (T = temperature, M = magenta/green, I = intensity). This is achieved as follows:
The 3-channel temperature is interpreted as the vector (T,M,I). The followiong scale values are then applied to the RGB components:
  outputR = inputR * (pow(2,I) + M/3 - T/2)
  outputG = inputG * (pow(2,I) - 2*M/3
  outputB = inputB * (pow(2,I) + M/3 + T/2)

File name of the texture applied to the light. If set to the empty string, no texture is applied. Any file format supported by OpenImageIO can be used. The texture is used in 2 ways - for looking up the texture value at the intersection point when a ray hits the light, and for building a lookup-table-based auxilliary data structure used for distributing light samples over the texture.
RGB value used when a texture lookup occurs outside the texture.
Texture scales in the u and v-directions.

The filtering mode to apply to the texture. Nearest neighbor is the cheapest filtering mode but produces a blocky result. Switch linear filtering on for a smoother result. Additionally, mip-mapping can be switched on with either nearest neighbor or linear filtering.
metadata.label: texture filter

metadata.comment: Whether to mirror the texture in the u-direction. If set to false, the texture is repeated in the u-direction.
Whether to mirror the texture in the v-direction. If set to false, the texture is repeated in the v-direction.
Number of times texture repeats in u over the scaled texture space.
Number of times texture repeats in v over the scaled texture space.
Clockwise rotation angle in degrees.

Translation of the texture in (u,v)-space, in units of the texture size. For example, a translation of (0.25, 0.5) will translate the texture one-quarter of its width in the u-direction and one-half of its height in the v-direction.

metadata.comment: The angle in degrees subtended by the DistantLight's diameter.
metadata.label: angular extent

metadata.comment:
The light's RGB values.
These are combined multiplicatively with the intensity and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.

Per-channel contrast used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. The operation mimics Nuke's ColorCorrect node's contrast function:
  For input >  0, output = 0.18 * pow(inputCompnent/0.18, contrast).
  For input <= 0, output = 0.18 * input * pow(1/0.18, contrast).

The light's exposure value.
This value provides an alternative to the intensity value as a mechanism for controlling the light's overall brightness, and is inspired by the corresponding photographic term but is generalised to apply independently to each light. To calculate its effect, pow(2, exposure) is combined multiplicatively with the color and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.

Per-channel gain used in tandem with a per-channel offset for color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel:
  output = input * gain + offset

Per-channel gamma used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel:
  For input >  0, output = pow(input, gamma)
  For input <= 0, output = input

The light's intensity.
This is combined multiplicatively with the color and other attributes in determining the light's 3-channel radiance.
Label used in light aov expressions.
Vector of LightFilters associated with the light.
metadata.label: light filters

metadata.comment:
The distance from the light beyond which a light-receiving surface will no longer receive shadows cast from that light.
Note that the distance is thresholded for each occlusion ray cast for this light, it is possible for a receiving point to lie at an intermediate distance such that some parts of the light are closer than the threshold distance and other parts beyond it, in which case the point will appearto be in partial shadow.
Whether motion-blur is active for this light. When set to true, the scene's illumination will correctly account for any blur() applied to the light's transformation matrix.

The distance from the light before which a light-receiving surface will no longer receive shadows cast from that light.
Note that the distance is thresholded for each occlusion ray cast for this light, it is possible for a receiving point to lie at an intermediate distance such that some parts of the light are closer than the threshold distance and other parts beyond it, in which case the point will appearto be in partial shadow.
The 4x4 matrix describing the transformation from local space to world space.
metadata.label: node xform

metadata.comment:
If set to true, a normalisation factor is applied to the light's radiance. The normalisation factor used is such that if a distant light of radiance (1,1,1) is directly overhead a Lambertian surface of colour (1,1,1), the  resulting outgoing radiance at the surface will be (1,1,1) regardless of the light's angular extent.
If set to false, the light's radiance is used as-is.

Per-channel offset used in tandem with a per-channel gain for color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel:
  output = input * gain + offset
Whether the light is switched on.

Switch this attribute on for shadows cast from this light to correctly respect presence values. When off, surfaces with a material with presence less than 1.0 will cast opaque shadows from this light. This is an optimization - when the attribute is off, occlusion rays (fast) are used for testing for shadows. When it is on, regular rays (slower) are used, and the material's presence is evaluated to determine how much shadowing should occur. When set to "use default" it reads from the value of SceneVariable enable_presence_shadows.
metadata.label: presence shadows

metadata.comment: Whether the light is used for ray termination color. Ray termination color is used for filling in falsely dark areas where ray paths have been terminated too early by the depth controls. Such a ray path immediately exits to any ray termination light(s) present in the light set being applied to the lobe, ignoring occlusion by scene geometry. Any light can either be a regular light or a ray termination light (but not both). Thus they can be freely assigned to light sets, which provides a mechanism for applying specific ray termination lights to specific materials, parts or objects. Ray termination color is only applied to non-hair transmission lobes.

Per-channel saturation used in color-correcting the light's texture, if one is present. This is achieved by applying the following formula for each channel:
  output = lerp(luminance(inputRGB), input, saturation).

Color temperature using Nuke-style T/M/I settings (T = temperature, M = magenta/green, I = intensity). This is achieved as follows:
The 3-channel temperature is interpreted as the vector (T,M,I). The followiong scale values are then applied to the RGB components:
  outputR = inputR * (pow(2,I) + M/3 - T/2)
  outputG = inputG * (pow(2,I) - 2*M/3
  outputB = inputB * (pow(2,I) + M/3 + T/2)

File name of the texture applied to the light. If set to the empty string, no texture is applied. Any file format supported by OpenImageIO can be used. The texture is used in 2 ways - for looking up the texture value at the intersection point when a ray hits the light, and for building a lookup-table-based auxilliary data structure used for distributing light samples over the texture.
RGB value used when a texture lookup occurs outside the texture.
Texture scales in the u and v-directions.

The filtering mode to apply to the texture. Nearest neighbor is the cheapest filtering mode but produces a blocky result. Switch linear filtering on for a smoother result. Additionally, mip-mapping can be switched on with either nearest neighbor or linear filtering.
metadata.label: texture filter

metadata.comment: Whether to mirror the texture in the u-direction. If set to false, the texture is repeated in the u-direction.
Whether to mirror the texture in the v-direction. If set to false, the texture is repeated in the v-direction.
Number of times texture repeats in u over the scaled texture space.
Number of times texture repeats in v over the scaled texture space.
Clockwise rotation angle in degrees.

Translation of the texture in (u,v)-space, in units of the texture size. For example, a translation of (0.25, 0.5) will translate the texture one-quarter of its width in the u-direction and one-half of its height in the v-direction.
Whether the light is visible in diffuse reflection.
metadata.label: visible diffuse reflection

metadata.label: visible glossy reflection

metadata.comment: [DreamWorks Animation internal] Enables or disables sending logging results to the Athena debugging database instead of the production database.
metadata.label: athena debug

metadata.comment: Specifies the order in which tiles (as areas of 8x8 pixels) are prioritized for batch rendering, which determines which areas of the image are rendered first. The ordering is not guaranteed: the strict sequence of tile starting and completion for any pass is nondeterministic due to thread scheduling.
metadata.label: batch tile order

metadata.comment: The square root of the number of samples taken for BSDF lobe evaluations on the primary intersection. The number of samples taken per material depends on the BSDF sampler strategy and the number of lobes that comprise the material.
metadata.label: bsdf samples

metadata.comment: The square root of the number of samples taken to evaluate BSSRDF (subsurface scattering) contributions on the primary intersection.
metadata.label: bssrdf samples

metadata.comment: This specifies the camera object used for rendering. If no camera is specified in the scene variables, MoonRay will render using the first camera object encountered.
Enables or disables checkpoint file writing.
metadata.label: checkpoint active

metadata.comment: When set to true, checkpoint file writes occur in a background thread that runs concurrently with the MCRT threads. Otherwise, all MCRT threads must wait while the checkpoint file is written.
metadata.label: checkpoint bg write

metadata.comment: Specifies the time interval, in minutes, between checkpoint file writes. The interval must be equal to or greater than 0.1 minutes.
metadata.label: checkpoint interval

metadata.comment: Specifies the maximum number of queued checkpoint images the checkpoint-writing background thread can handle. The value of checkpoint_max_bgcache must be greater than or equal to 1. If the number of queued checkpoint images exceeds this limit, MCRT threads will be temporarily suspended while background images are written to make room in the queue. A larger value can support background writing even with short checkpoint intervals, but it may require more memory. A value of 2 is recommended for most cases.
metadata.label: checkpoint max bgcache

metadata.comment: Specifies the maximum fraction of the snapshot overhead threshold for an extra snapshot action in the event of an unexpected interruption by SIGINT. The value is expressed as a fraction. If the value is set to zero or a negative number, no extra snapshot action will be executed, and no checkpoint file will be generated if SIGINT is received.
metadata.label: checkpoint max snapshot overhead

metadata.comment: Allows you to choose whether checkpoint images are written based on time elapsed or on quality reached.
metadata.label: checkpoint mode

metadata.comment: When set to true, the last checkpoint file will be overwritten when writing out the new checkpoint file. If set to false, the checkpoint filename will be appended with the total number of samples, which will result in the retention of all checkpoint files.
metadata.label: checkpoint overwrite

metadata.comment: Specifies the filename of a Lua script that will be executed after every checkpoint file is written. The script will run concurrently with the ongoing MCRT threads. For more information, refer to the documentation for MoonRay-provided Lua variables accessible within the script.
metadata.label: checkpoint post script

metadata.comment: Specifies the number of quality steps, which refers to the internal sampling iteration count between checkpoint file writes. The value must be equal to or greater than 1. In the case of uniform sampling, this number of steps is equivalent to the pixel sampling steps for each pixel. For example, if you set quality steps to 2, a checkpoint file will be created every time each pixel's sample count exceeds 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and so on. In the case of adaptive sampling, this number of steps is equivalent to the internal adaptive sampling iteration steps. A recommended number falls within the range of 1 to 3. For example, if you set the value to 2, a checkpoint file will be created after finishing every 2 adaptive sampling passes. A larger value will conduct more rendering passes before writing a file.
metadata.label: checkpoint quality steps

metadata.comment: Causes the render to finish based on the total pixel sample count. For example, if the value is 1024, the render will end after the next checkpoint write when each pixel exceeds 1024 samples. If the value is set to 0, the sample cap feature is disabled.
metadata.label: checkpoint sample cap

metadata.comment: Specifies the time interval, in minutes, allowed for a snapshot when a SIGINT is encountered. If the value is 0 or negative, the checkpoint_max_snapshot_overhead parameter is used instead.
metadata.label: checkpoint snapshot interval

metadata.comment: Specifies the samples per pixel (SPP). A checkpoint file is created when all pixels' SPP are greater than or equal to this number. A checkpoint file is created once this criterion is met.
metadata.label: checkpoint start sample

metadata.comment: Specifies the order in which tiles (as areas of 8x8 pixels) are prioritized for checkpoint rendering, which determines which areas of the image are rendered first. The ordering is not guaranteed: the strict sequence of tile starting and completion for any pass is nondeterministic due to thread scheduling.
metadata.label: checkpoint tile order

metadata.comment: Determines when the render will finish based on the total render process time in minutes. If the value is exceeded, the render will finish after the next checkpoint write. If the value is set to 0, the time cap feature is disabled.
metadata.label: checkpoint time cap

metadata.comment:
This variable specifies the total number of checkpoint files for the quality-based checkpoint mode. It serves as a substitute parameter for checkpoint_quality_steps. If the value is set to 0 (the default), the interval at which checkpoints are generated is controlled by the checkpoint_quality_steps variable. If the value is set to 1 or higher, the renderer will attempt to automatically generate a user-defined number of checkpoint files based on this value. This option takes into account the checkpoint_start_sample variable.

In some cases, the renderer may be unable to create the requested number of checkpoint_total_files due to limitations in the internal implementation or because the user has specified a value greater than 1 for the checkpoint_start_sample variable. However, in these cases, the renderer will attempt to generate the closest possible number of checkpoint files to the user-defined value.
metadata.label: checkpoint total files

metadata.comment: Names of primitive attribute containing crypto UVs
metadata.label: crypto UV attribute name

metadata.comment: Determines whether to record presence bounces as separate cryptomatte samples.

Specifies the port number for the debug console. When the debug console functionalities are enabled, you can use a telnet connection to send commands and control rendering behavior for debugging purposes.
- A value of -1 disables all debug console functionality.
- A positive value specifies a specific port number.
- If you set the port number to 0, the kernel will find an available port for you and display the port number to stderr.
metadata.label: debug console

metadata.comment: Allows for rendering a single pixel and is typically used for debugging. The value given specifies the 2D pixel coordinate expressed from the bottom-left of the frame-viewport
metadata.label: debug pixel

metadata.comment: Deprecated.
metadata.label: debug rays depth range

metadata.comment: Deprecated.
metadata.label: debug rays file

metadata.comment: Deprecated.
metadata.label: debug rays primary range

metadata.comment: Maximum curvature (in degrees) of the deep surface within a pixel before it is split
metadata.label: deep curvature tolerance

Deep image format:
		openexr2.0: vanilla OpenEXR deep
		opendcx2.0: DCX abuffer mask encoding
metadata.label: deep format

metadata.comment: Names of primitive attributes containing deep IDs
metadata.label: deep ID attribute names

metadata.comment: Volume opacity compression resolution.  Lower values gives higher compression.
metadata.label: deep vol compression res

metadata.comment: Maximum range of the deep surface's Z values within a pixel before it is split
metadata.label: deep z tolerance

metadata.comment: This attribute specifies a camera to use for adaptive geometry tessellation. The rendering camera is used if no camera is specified.
Forces all hair materials to sample each hair BSDF lobe independently. This will enable the LPE label syntax for 'hair R', 'hair TT', 'hair TRT' and 'hair TRRT ' but will result in slower rendering
metadata.label: disable optimized hair sampling

metadata.comment: Enables or disables geometry displacement.
metadata.label: enable displacement

metadata.comment: Enables or disables camera depth-of-field (DOF)
metadata.label: enable DOF

metadata.comment: Specifies whether the max_geometry_resolution limit is in effect.
metadata.label: enable max geometry resolution

metadata.comment: Enables or disables motion blur
metadata.label: enable motion blur

metadata.comment: Whether or not to respect a material's "presence" value for shadow rays. Performance may improve when disabled, but all materials are treated as fully present.
metadata.label: enable presence shadows

metadata.comment: Enables or disables shadowing through occlusion rays.
metadata.label: enable shadowing

metadata.comment: Enables or disables sub-surface scattering.
metadata.label: enable subsurface scattering

metadata.comment: Metadata that is passed directly to the exr header. Format: {"name", "type", "value"}
metadata.label: exr header attributes

metadata.comment: If this flag is off, the tessellation related data for subdivision surface will be deleted after tessellation is done. This is to save memory for single frame rendering. Otherwise, that data will be kept in memory to support re-tessellation after geometry are updated.
metadata.label: fast geometry update

metadata.comment: The color to use for materials or map shaders that are unable to execute shading, usually due to incomplete initialization.
metadata.label: fatal color

metadata.comment: (Frames per second) Affects motion blur.
Used to provide unique samples per frame, and for selecting the frame for scenes with animated data.
The desired height of the output image(s), in pixels.
metadata.label: image height

metadata.comment: The desired width of the output image(s), in pixels.
metadata.label: image width

metadata.comment: This specifies the layer object used for rendering. If no layer is specified in the scene variables, MoonRay will rendering using the first layer object encountered.
The square root of the number of samples taken for each light on the primary intersection.
metadata.label: light samples

metadata.comment: Controls which light sampling scheme to use:  uniform or adaptive
metadata.label: light sampling mode

metadata.comment: When the light sampling mode is 'adaptive', this attribute controls how many lights are sampled per light sample, where 0.0 is low quality (1 light sampled per light sample) and 1.0 is high quality (all lights sampled per light sample). Any value in between will cause adaptive light sampling to kick into effect, meaning that it will choose a higher or lower number of lights depending on what that particular point needs. A number closer to 0.0 will cause it to sample a lower number of lights on average, and vice versa.
metadata.label: light sampling quality

metadata.comment: Globally enables or disables lights being visible in camera. Each light has its own setting which may override this value.
metadata.label: lights visible in camera

metadata.comment: By default, the random number generators are seeded by considering the frame number. However, if lock_frame_noise is true, the same seed values are used for each frame, which is typically undesirable.
metadata.label: lock frame noise

metadata.comment: Determines whether debugging-level messages are logged.
Determines whether information-level messages are logged.
Used only in arras moonray context, automatically set by arras and indicates the MCRT computation ID in the current session
metadata.label: machine id

metadata.comment: When adaptive sampling is turned on, this represents the max number of samples we can throw at a pixel. It's best to err on the high side since adaptive sampling will cull out samples where they're not needed based on the target adaptive error, in which case we should rarely hit the max samples value.
metadata.label: max adaptive samples

metadata.comment: The maximum ray depth (number of "bounces") for diffuse|glossy|mirror event types. This can be thought of as the global depth limit. Reducing this can improve performance at the cost of biasing the rendered image.
metadata.label: max depth

metadata.comment: The maximum ray depth (number of "bounces") for diffuse event types. Reducing this can improve performance at the cost of biasing the rendered image. Note that this limit is also governed by the global "max depth" attribute.
metadata.label: max diffuse depth

metadata.comment: Used to provide unique samples per frame.
metadata.label: max frame

metadata.comment: Specifies a global limit to geometry resolution. Geometry procedurals should respect this limit.
metadata.label: max geometry resolution

metadata.comment: The maximum ray depth (number of "bounces") for glossy event types. Reducing this can improve performance at the cost of biasing the rendered image. Note that this limit is also governed by the global "max depth" attribute.
metadata.label: max glossy depth

metadata.comment: The maximum ray depth (number of "bounces") for hair material types. This limit may need to be increased to allow for more hair-to-hair interactions, especially for blonde/white hair or fur. Reducing this can improve performance at the cost of biasing the rendered image.
metadata.label: max hair depth

metadata.comment: The maximum ray depth (number of "bounces") for mirror event types. Reducing this can improve performance at the cost of biasing the rendered image. Note that this limit is also governed by the global "max depth" attribute.
metadata.label: max mirror depth

metadata.comment: The maximum ray depth (number of "bounces") for presence event types. The material's "presence" attribute is ignored after this depth has been reached and the surface is treated as fully present. Reducing this can improve performance at the cost of biasing the rendered image.
metadata.label: max presence depth

metadata.comment: The maximum ray depth (number of "bounces") to allow subsurface scattering. For ray depths beyond this limit Lambertian diffuse is used to approximate subsurface scattering.
metadata.label: max subsurface per path

metadata.comment: The maximum ray depth (number of "bounces") for volume event types. Volumes are ignored after this depth has been reached. Reducing this can improve performance at the cost of biasing the rendered image.
metadata.label: max volume depth

metadata.comment: This is the minimum number of samples taken per pixel before enabling adaptive sampling. A larger number of samples may prevent the adaptive sampler from prematurely identifying an area as converged but may incur a longer running time.
metadata.label: min adaptive samples

metadata.comment: Used to provide unique samples per frame.
metadata.label: min frame

metadata.comment: Frame-relative time offsets for motion sampling
metadata.label: motion steps

metadata.comment: Used only in arras moonray context, automatically set by arras and indicates total number of MCRT computations active in the current session
metadata.label: num machines

metadata.comment: When using resumable rendering, the Lua script named here is executed after the render prep stage. In addition, MoonRay sets some Lua global variables the script can access. This functionality is disabled when the script name is empty or when not using resumable rendering. Please refer to the checkpoint/resume documentation for more details.
metadata.label: on resume script

metadata.comment: This specifies the output path for the beauty image (RGBA). This is independent of the AOV RenderOutputs, which can also write a beauty image.
metadata.label: output file

metadata.comment: The type of filter used for filter importance sampling. A box filter with a width of 1 is analogous to disabling pixel filtering.
metadata.label: pixel filter

metadata.comment: The overall extents, in pixels, of the pixel filter. Larger values will result in softer images.
metadata.label: pixel filter width

metadata.comment: The square root of the number of primary samples taken for each pixel in uniform sampling mode. For example, a value of 4 will result in 4*4 = 16 uniform pixel samples.
metadata.label: pixel samples

metadata.comment: The presence quality defines the threshold for path throughput after which presence sampling becomes stochastic. This is similar to russian roulette.  A value of 1.0 means never use stochastic sampling (highest quality).  A value of 0.0 means always use stochastic sampling (faster, but may be noisy).  Values between 0.0 and 1.0 will generally be a good trade-off in speed vs. quality when multiple layers of presence are involved.
metadata.label: presence quality

metadata.comment: The presence threshold defines the point at which the accumulated presence can be considered opaque, skipping the generation of presence continuation rays.
metadata.label: presence threshold

metadata.comment: The aov that acts as the primary output. If undefined, it will default to the typical render buffer.

Specifies the order in which tiles (as areas of 8x8 pixels) are prioritized for progressive rendering, which determines which areas of the image are rendered first. The ordering is not guaranteed: the strict sequence of tile starting and completion for any pass is nondeterministic due to thread scheduling.
metadata.label: progressive tile order

metadata.comment: turns on/off propagation for ray visibility masks
metadata.label: propagate visibility bounce type

metadata.comment: Window that is rendered. Overrides image width / height (and overrides aperture window override). Order: xmin ymin xmax ymax, with origin at left bottom.
metadata.label: region window

metadata.comment: Final divisor for the overall image dimensions. A quick way to reduce or increase the size of the render. A value of 2 halves the size of the rendered image(s). A value of 0.5 doubles it.
make aov output as resumable for resume render
metadata.label: resumable output

metadata.comment: resuming render process
metadata.label: resume render

metadata.comment: Clamp material roughness along paths. A value of 1 clamps values to the maximum roughness encountered, while lower values temper the clamping value. 0 disables the effect. Using this technique reduces fireflies from indirect caustics but is biased.
metadata.label: roughness clamping factor

metadata.comment: The Russian roulette threshold specifies the point at which point Russian roulette is evaluated for direct light sampling and BSDF continuation. The unit is luminance of the radiance.
metadata.label: russian roulette threshold

metadata.comment: Clamp sample values only after the given non-specular ray depth.
metadata.label: sample clamping depth

metadata.comment: Clamp sample radiance values to this maximum value (the feature is disabled if the value is 0.0). Using this technique reduces fireflies, but is biased.
metadata.label: sample clamping value

metadata.comment: Controls which sampling scheme to use: uniform or adaptive.
metadata.label: sampling mode

metadata.comment: (in meters): one unit in world space = 'scene scale' meters
metadata.label: scene scale

metadata.comment: Attempt to soften hard shadow terminator boundaries due to shading/geometric normal deviations.  "ON uses a custom terminator softening method. Cosine Compensation" is Chiang's 2019 SIGGRAPH technique.  "GGX" is Estevez's raytracing gems technique.  "Sine Compensation" is a sine based modification of Chiang's method. Different scenes may work better with different techniques.  The recommendation is to start with the custom compensation ON, then sine compensation technique, then GGX, then cosine.
metadata.label: shadow terminator fix

metadata.comment: If use_rotation_motion_blur is false this will use slerp to interpolate the node_xform for motion blur
metadata.label: slerp xforms

metadata.comment: The filename to write the rendering statistics to in CSV format.
metadata.label: stats file

metadata.comment: Subviewport of region window. Coordinate (0,0) maps to left, bottom of region window
metadata.label: sub viewport

metadata.comment: When adaptive sampling is turned on, this represents the desired quality of the output images. Lower values will give higher quality but take longer to render. Higher values will give lower quality but render quicker.
metadata.label: target adaptive error

metadata.comment: Used only in arras moonray context, defines the task distribution method to the MCRT computation. Multi-plex pixel is the default and preferred method. Non-overlapped tile is experimental and only used for debugging/development purposes
metadata.label: task distribution type

metadata.comment: Adjusts the amount of texture filtering.
metadata.label: texture blur

metadata.comment: Specifies the maximum size of the texture cache in megabytes. This value can significantly impact rendering speed, where larger values often improve rendering speed.
metadata.label: texture cache size

metadata.comment: Specifies the maximum number of simultaneous open texture file handles.
metadata.label: texture file handles

metadata.comment: Define temporary directory name for temporary file generation. Use $TMPDIR environment variable value if this variable is empty.If $TMPDIR is also empty, use /tmp
metadata.label: tmp dir

metadata.comment: The transparency threshold defines the point at which the accumulated opacity can be considered opaque, skipping the generation of new transparency rays.
metadata.label: transparency threshold

metadata.comment:
Specifies whether to use a two-stage writing process for images. In two-stage writing, the image is first written to a temporary location and then moved to the final location. This approach significantly reduces the risk of output data corruption due to an unexpected render process termination.
The directory where the temporary files are stored is defined by the "tmp_dir" scene variable.
metadata.label: two stage output

metadata.comment: Checks geometry for bad data
metadata.label: validate geometry

metadata.comment: Controls how volume attenuation gets exponentially scaled down when rendering multiple scattering volumes. Dialing down the value generally results in more translucent look. This variable is only effective when "max volume depth" is greater than 1
metadata.label: volume attenuation factor

metadata.comment: Controls how scattering contribution gets exponentially scaled down when rendering multiple scattering volumes. Dialing down the value generally results in a darker volume scattering look. This variable is only effective when "max volume depth" is greater than 1
metadata.label: volume contribution factor

metadata.comment: Sample number along the ray when computing volume scattering radiance towards the eye. Set to 0 to turn off volume lighting completely.
metadata.label: volume illumination samples

metadata.comment: Number of indirect illumination samples on volumes (per primary ray).
metadata.label: volume indirect samples

metadata.comment: As a ray travels through volumes, it will accumulate opacity. When the value exceeds the volume opacity threshold, the renderer will stop further volume integration along this ray.
metadata.label: volume opacity threshold

metadata.comment:
Selects how to handle contributions from overlapping volumes:
		sum: add contributions from all volumes
		max: only consider maximum volume based on extinction
		rnd: randomly choose one value weighted by extinction
		Warning: light linking does not work correctly in sum mode.
metadata.label: volume overlap mode

metadata.comment: Controls how phase function (anisotropy) gets exponentially scaled down when rendering multiple scattering volumes. This variable is only effective when "max volume depth" is greater than 1
metadata.label: volume phase attenuation factor

metadata.comment: Controls the overall quality of volume rendering. The higher number gives better volume shape detail and more accurate scattering integration result.
metadata.label: volume quality

metadata.comment: Controls the quality of volume shadow (transmittance). The higher number gives more accurate volume shadow.
metadata.label: volume shadow quality
